Start a project version

Source: R/initialize_project.R
initialize_project.Rd

initialize_project() sets the paths of a project version and sources its functions folder. It MUST be the first call in every vNN_run.R.

Usage

initialize_project(
  version,
  home,
  folders,
  env = .GlobalEnv,
  one_file = NULL,
  fake_real_data = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

version

The version, written as "v" and two digits, for example "v01".

home

The project folder. It holds <version>_run.R, <version>_functions/ and the file of the rules pbn.yml.

folders

The folders outside the project that the project reads, as a named character vector, for example c(main = "../data", lookup = "../codes"). One folder MAY have no name, and it then gets the name main. Each name MUST be a syntactic R name, once. A folder MAY be absent, for example on a computer without the real data. Only save_results() for the scenario "real" then stops.

env

The environment that the functions folder is sourced into.

one_file

NULL. The file of to_one_file() gives a value here. Do not write it by hand. See the section One file.

fake_real_data

TRUE when the folders of folders on this computer hold fake files in the formats of the real data, and FALSE, the default, otherwise. See the section Fake real data.

...

Nothing. A call with the removed argument data_raw stops, and the error says how to use folders.

Value

Invisibly, a list with version, home, results and folders. results is the results folder, and folders the named paths of the folders.

Details

initialize_project() does these steps in this order:

  1. It reads the rules of check_project() from home/pbn.yml. It stops on each error of pbn.yml that stops check_project(), also when the file is missing.

  2. It computes the md5 of <version>_run.R and of each file in <version>_functions/, before it sources them. save_results() stores them in manifest$source_md5, without <version>_functions/blocks.R.

  3. It lists each file under each folder of folders that exists, at any depth, with its size and its modification time. This is the fingerprint of the data. pbn never reads the content of a data file, so a file of 60 GB costs what a small file costs. save_results() stores the fingerprint in manifest$data_files of the scenario "real". A file that the run writes later is not in the list. The section The fingerprint of the data gives the rules.

  4. It calls org::initialize_project() with folders_to_be_sourced set to <version>_functions. max_loc_per_file is the limit of the rule loc_per_file, 1000 in the house set. When the rule is warn or off, it is Inf, because the check of org stops the run on a file with more lines. pbn gives org no folder of folders, so org::project holds home, computer_id and env only.

Project code finds a folder with folder(), for example file.path(pbn::folder("main"), "d.csv"). Call folder() inside a function: a top-level call in a file of the functions folder runs before initialize_project() sets the folders, and it stops.

The results folder is <home>/<version>_results. save_results() creates it. initialize_project() creates no folder, also no folder with today's date. It stops when <version>_functions/ does not exist.

initialize_project() reads no scenario, no simulation, no command-line argument and no environment variable, and it sets no seed. scenarios() chooses the scenarios, and add_data() and add_analyses() set the seeds.

The fingerprint of the data

The fingerprint is a data.frame with one row for each file, sorted by file in the C locale:

  • file, the name <folder name>/<path in the folder> with /, for example main/sub/d.csv. It never holds the path of the folder.

  • size, the size in bytes.

  • mtime, the modification time in whole seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, with the fraction of a second cut off. A copy of a file can lose part of that fraction, for example on Windows, and whole seconds stay the same.

Hidden files count. A link to a file gives the size and the time of its target, and list.files() follows a link to a folder. A broken link stops initialize_project(). It also stops when a folder of folders is inside another or is the same folder. It stops when a folder holds or is inside <version>_results/ or <version>_cache_gitexclude/, because pbn writes there in each run. A folder elsewhere inside home is allowed.

A file that changed in place, and kept its size and the second of its modification time, is not seen. A copy that does not keep the modification times looks like changed data, so the cache computes the data again. file.copy(..., copy.date = TRUE) keeps them.

Fake real data

The real data of a project MAY be on a server only. Its folders on this computer MAY then hold fake files in the formats of the real data. Then the code that reads the real data runs here, and check_one_file() has results to compare. Give fake_real_data = TRUE in the run script of such a computer. It is about the scenario "real" only:

  • The manifest of the real results gets fake_real_data = TRUE. It is FALSE without the flag. A fake scenario has no such field.

  • The run log says that the scenario real ran on fake real data, in the sections Run and History. The sections Data and Exclusions name the scenario real (fake real data).

  • make_outputs() writes the output of "real" as fake output, into real/output_fake_data/ with the prefix fake_data_, and stamp_fake() marks its figures. It deletes an old real/output/.

  • show_blocks() and show_block() print FAKE REAL DATA.

The argument decides only what save_results() writes into the manifest. make_outputs(), stamp_fake(), show_blocks() and show_block() read fake_real_data from the manifest of the real results on the disk. So an R session without the argument still marks such results, and an R session with it never marks results from real data.

  • The rule real_results_are_fake of check_project() warns while such real results are on the disk.

read_results() reads such results as usual. The file of to_one_file() never gives fake_real_data, because the server holds the real data. fake_real_data = TRUE together with one_file stops.

One file

The file of to_one_file() calls initialize_project() with one_file, a list with these elements:

  • project, the name of the project folder on the computer that made the file. The run log names the project with it.

  • source_md5, the md5 of the run script and of each file of the functions folder on that computer. The manifest stores it.

  • code, the code of the functions folder as one quoted block, in the order that org sources the files.

With one_file, initialize_project() reads no pbn.yml, needs no functions folder, and checks no code lines. It evaluates code in env in the place of the source of the functions folder. A use of the cache then does not check the data_*.R files on the disk, because the code is in the file.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other project setup: end_unless_real(), folder(), scenarios()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_initialize_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines("extends: house_2026_11_17", file.path(home, "pbn.yml"))
writeLines(
  "CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = c(1, 3)))",
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)

env <- new.env()
p <- pbn::initialize_project(
  version = "v01",
  home = home,
  folders = c(main = file.path(home, "data")),
  env = env
)
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/RtmppiM411/pbn_initialize_example/v01_functions into 
p$results
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmppiM411/pbn_initialize_example/v01_results"
pbn::folder("main")
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmppiM411/pbn_initialize_example/data"
env$CFG$scenarios
#>   scenario sims
#> 1     real    1
#> 2     null    3

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
